title: India's AI Funding Nearly Doubles to $1.6 Billion, With Mumbai Ahead of Bengaluru
excerpt: Tracxn's India AI - 9M 2026 Report puts Mumbai first with $765 million and Bengaluru second with $711 million, as funding concentrates into fewer, far larger rounds.
body:
• Indian AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in January-September 2026, up 96% from $822 million in the same period last year, according to Tracxn's India AI - 9M 2026 Report.
  • Mumbai took the largest share with $765 million (48% of the total), ahead of Bengaluru's $711 million (44%) and Chennai's $75.5 million (about 5%); the three cities together accounted for around 96% of all AI investment.
  • The money concentrated sharply: 87 funding rounds, down 42% from 149 a year earlier, while the average deal size rose to $18.5 million from $5.5 million, and the ten largest rounds raised $1.5 billion — 90% of the total.
  • For diaspora investors tracking India's AI sector, the report's caution matters: India raised just 0.4% of the $383.5 billion invested in AI worldwide in the period, ranking ninth among countries.

Indian AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding between January and September 2026, a 96 per cent increase from the $822 million raised in the same period last year and a 162 per cent jump from the $616 million raised in the corresponding period of 2024, according to Tracxn's India AI - 9M 2026 Report, reported by India Today.

Mumbai moves ahead of Bengaluru

Mumbai emerged as the country's biggest AI funding hub with $765 million, 48 per cent of the national total — a sharp increase from the $15.7 million the city raised in the same period last year, when it accounted for just 2 per cent of India's AI funding. Two deals drove the jump: Mumbai-based AI cloud provider Neysa raised $600 million in a Series B round in February, the largest AI funding deal in the country during the period and, on its own, around 37 per cent of India's total AI funding; Yotta raised $150 million in a Series D round in July.

Bengaluru, long India's startup capital, took second place with $711 million, 44 per cent of the total, down from a 54 per cent share in the first nine months of 2025. Generative AI startup Sarvam raised $255 million in a Series B round in June and a further $90.4 million in August, and Emergent was among the other prominent Bengaluru companies to attract investors. Chennai ranked third with $75.5 million, about 5 per cent of the total, most of it from Freehand's $75 million Series B round. Together, the three cities accounted for around 96 per cent of all AI investment raised in India during the period.

Fewer, much larger cheques

The sector recorded 87 funding rounds in the first nine months of 2026, down 42 per cent from 149 in the same period last year, while the average deal size increased to $18.5 million from $5.5 million. The ten largest rounds together raised $1.5 billion, 90 per cent of the period's total. Tracxn data shared with ET AI put the same concentration in deal terms: Neysa's $600 million, Sarvam's $255 million, Yotta's $150 million and Emergent's $130 million together accounted for 72 per cent of the total, and AI infrastructure alone raised $1.2 billion across 19 rounds.

"AI funding has risen in dollars but not in the number of deals, and almost all of the rise comes from AI infrastructure rounds."

— Neha Singh, co-founder of Tracxn, to ET AI

By stage, early-stage funding jumped 191 per cent to $1.3 billion, from $434 million a year earlier, and accounted for 78 per cent of total funding, compared with 53 per cent in the first nine months of 2025. Late-stage funding rose a modest 4 per cent to $280 million, while seed-stage investment declined 42 per cent to $69.2 million. A total of 111 investors participated, down 34 per cent from 169 a year earlier, and first-time investors fell 39 per cent to 43. Peak XV Partners led early-stage investors with three investments, followed by Prosus and Khosla Ventures with two each.

Three new unicorns, and the global gap

The funding produced three new AI unicorns in the first nine months of 2026 — Neysa, Sarvam and Emergent crossed the $1 billion valuation mark, compared with one new AI unicorn in the corresponding period last year. Indian AI companies recorded six acquisitions, against five a year earlier, and no public listings during the period.

The global comparison is the sobering part of the report. Worldwide, AI companies raised $383.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026; India's $1.6 billion was 0.4 per cent of that total, placing the country ninth. As India Today's report concluded, the concentration of funding in a few companies and cities, alongside the fall in the number of deals and investors, suggests the funding boom has not yet reached the wider startup ecosystem.
nri_angle: For diaspora investors, the Tracxn figures show India's AI money concentrating in Mumbai and Bengaluru infrastructure deals, while India still takes just 0.4% of global AI funding.
author: Diaspora Desk
